DIVISION_BY_ZERO.title: Division by Zero
DIVISION_BY_ZERO.beginner_explanation: The code attempts to divide an integer by zero.
DIVISION_BY_ZERO.why_it_happened: Java does not allow integer division by zero. The compiler detects this invalid constant expression.
common_causes: Dividing an integer literal directly by 0 (e.g. 10 / 0)
Evaluating a constant expression where the denominator is 0
Using modulo by zero (e.g. 10 % 0)
DIVISION_BY_ZERO.suggested_fix: Use a non-zero divisor, or validate the divisor before dividing.
DIVISION_BY_ZERO.prevention_advice: Always make sure an integer divisor cannot be zero before performing integer division.

INCOMPATIBLE_TYPES.title: Type Mismatch
INCOMPATIBLE_TYPES.beginner_explanation: You are trying to store a value in a variable whose declared type cannot hold that value. Java is strongly typed, meaning an `int` variable can only hold integers, not text (`String`).
INCOMPATIBLE_TYPES.why_it_happened: Java enforces strict type safety at compile time. When you assign a String (enclosed in double quotes) to an integer variable, the compiler prevents potential runtime crashes by stopping compilation immediately.
common_causes: Quoting numbers as text (e.g. "20" instead of 20)
Assigning floating point numbers (e.g. 3.14) to integer variables without casting
Calling a method that returns one type and assigning it to another incompatible type
INCOMPATIBLE_TYPES.suggested_fix: Change the value to match the variable's type, or parse/convert the value if needed (e.g., `Integer.parseInt("20")`).
INCOMPATIBLE_TYPES.prevention_advice: Remember: numbers without quotes (20) are integers; text inside quotes ("20") is a String. When accepting user text input, parse it explicitly with `Integer.parseInt()` or `Double.parseDouble()`.

SEMICOLON_EXPECTED.title: Missing Semicolon
SEMICOLON_EXPECTED.beginner_explanation: Java statements must always end with a semicolon (`;`). You missed a semicolon at the end of the line or statement.
SEMICOLON_EXPECTED.why_it_happened: In Java, semicolons act like periods at the end of sentences. The compiler uses semicolons to know where one command ends and the next begins.
common_causes: Forgetting to add ';' at the end of variable declarations or method calls
Accidentally typing a colon ':' or comma ',' instead of a semicolon ';'
SEMICOLON_EXPECTED.suggested_fix: Append a semicolon `;` to the end of the statement.
SEMICOLON_EXPECTED.prevention_advice: Get into the habit of ending every variable assignment, method call, and return statement with a semicolon. Statements inside loops and conditionals also need semicolons.

CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_VARIABLE.title: Undefined Variable
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_VARIABLE.beginner_explanation: Java does not recognize the variable name you referenced. It hasn't been declared, was misspelled, or is outside the current scope.
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_VARIABLE.why_it_happened: Before you can read or modify a variable in Java, you must declare it with a type (e.g., `int value = 10;`). Java also cares about case sensitivity (`Value` is different from `value`).
common_causes: Typo in the variable name (e.g., `myVar` vs `myvar`)
Using the variable before declaring it
Declaring the variable inside an `if` block or loop (local scope) and trying to access it outside
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_VARIABLE.suggested_fix: Declare the variable with its type before using it, or verify that the spelling matches the original declaration.
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_VARIABLE.prevention_advice: Always declare variables before using them, double check spelling and capitalization, and check variable scope.

CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_METHOD.title: Undefined Method
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_METHOD.beginner_explanation: Java cannot find the method you are trying to call. The method either doesn't exist, has a typo, or belongs to a different class.
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_METHOD.why_it_happened: Java verifies every method call against the class definition. If the method name does not match any declared method in the class, compilation halts.
common_causes: Misspelling the method name (e.g. `System.out.printline()` instead of `println()`)
Calling a method without importing its required package
Calling an instance method without creating an object instance
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_METHOD.suggested_fix: Check the spelling of the method name and verify it exists on the target class or object.
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_METHOD.prevention_advice: Check the exact documentation for library methods. Method names in Java typically use camelCase.

CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_CLASS.title: Undefined Class or Missing Import
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_CLASS.beginner_explanation: The compiler cannot find the class you referenced. You likely need to import the class from a package.
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_CLASS.why_it_happened: Java only automatically imports classes from `java.lang`. Classes like `Scanner`, `ArrayList`, or `List` must be explicitly imported from `java.util`.
common_causes: Missing `import java.util.Scanner;` or other package imports
Typo in class name (e.g., `Scaner` instead of `Scanner`)
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_CLASS.example_fixed:
import java.util.Scanner;

Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_CLASS.suggested_fix: Add the appropriate `import` statement at the top of your Java file.
CANNOT_FIND_SYMBOL_CLASS.prevention_advice: Whenever using utility classes like `Scanner`, `List`, `ArrayList`, or `HashMap`, add their import statement at the top of your file.

METHOD_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH.title: Wrong Method Arguments
METHOD_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH.beginner_explanation: You called a method with the wrong number or wrong types of arguments.
METHOD_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH.why_it_happened: Java methods require parameters that exactly match the method declaration. Passing the wrong type or number of arguments will cause the compiler to reject the call.
common_causes: Passing too many or too few arguments
Passing arguments in the wrong order
Passing a String when a number or boolean was expected
METHOD_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH.suggested_fix: Provide the arguments matching the method's expected parameter types and count.
METHOD_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH.prevention_advice: Check the method definition or documentation to see what arguments it expects.

VARIABLE_NOT_INITIALIZED.title: Variable Might Not Have Been Initialized
VARIABLE_NOT_INITIALIZED.beginner_explanation: You are trying to use a local variable before giving it a starting value.
VARIABLE_NOT_INITIALIZED.why_it_happened: Unlike instance fields which get default values (like 0 or null), local variables declared inside methods do not have default values. Java requires them to be assigned before they are read.
common_causes: Declaring `int x;` and using `x` without writing `x = 5;` first
Assigning the variable only inside an `if` block that might not execute
VARIABLE_NOT_INITIALIZED.suggested_fix: Initialize the variable with a default value (e.g. `0`, `""`, or `null`) when declaring it.
VARIABLE_NOT_INITIALIZED.prevention_advice: Initialize local variables when you declare them: `int total = 0;`.

MISSING_RETURN_STATEMENT.title: Missing Return Statement
MISSING_RETURN_STATEMENT.beginner_explanation: Your method specifies a return type other than `void`, but reaches the end without returning a value.
MISSING_RETURN_STATEMENT.why_it_happened: Every execution path in a non-void method must end with a valid `return` statement that produces a value of the declared type.
common_causes: Having `return` inside an `if` branch but not in the corresponding `else` branch
Declaring `int myMethod()` instead of `void myMethod()`
MISSING_RETURN_STATEMENT.suggested_fix: Add a `return` statement returning the expected type, or change the return type to `void` if the method shouldn't return anything.
MISSING_RETURN_STATEMENT.prevention_advice: Ensure all code branches (including `else` statements and after loops) return a value.

STATIC_CONTEXT_ERROR.title: Non-Static Member Referenced From Static Context
STATIC_CONTEXT_ERROR.beginner_explanation: You tried to access a normal instance variable or method directly from a `static` method like `main` without creating an object first.
STATIC_CONTEXT_ERROR.why_it_happened: `static` methods belong to the class itself, not to any individual object instance. They cannot access non-static members because there is no specific object instance (`this`) attached.
common_causes: Calling a helper method from `main` without declaring the helper method as `static`
Accessing a class field inside `main` that wasn't declared `static`
STATIC_CONTEXT_ERROR.suggested_fix: Make the member `static`, or create an instance of the class (e.g. `Main obj = new Main(); obj.score`).
STATIC_CONTEXT_ERROR.prevention_advice: When writing small standalone programs with `main`, declare helper methods and variables as `static` unless modeling objects.

LOSSY_CONVERSION.title: Possible Lossy Conversion
LOSSY_CONVERSION.beginner_explanation: You are assigning a larger data type (like `double` or `long`) to a smaller data type (like `int` or `float`), which could lose data (like decimal places).
LOSSY_CONVERSION.why_it_happened: Java protects you from unintentionally losing precision. Converting `3.99` to an `int` would truncate the `.99`, so Java requires an explicit cast.
common_causes: Assigning a decimal number (`double`) to an `int` variable
Assigning a `long` to an `int` without casting
LOSSY_CONVERSION.suggested_fix: Change the variable type to `double`, or explicitly cast the value using `(int)`.
LOSSY_CONVERSION.prevention_advice: Use `double` for values with decimal points and `int` for whole numbers.

PARENTHESIS_EXPECTED.title: Unmatched Parenthesis
PARENTHESIS_EXPECTED.beginner_explanation: You opened a parenthesis `(` without closing it `)`, or closed one without opening it.
PARENTHESIS_EXPECTED.why_it_happened: All parentheses in Java expressions and method parameter lists must be paired symmetrically.
common_causes: Missing `)` at the end of a method call or `if` condition
Extra `)` accidentally typed in an arithmetic expression
PARENTHESIS_EXPECTED.suggested_fix: Ensure every opening `(` has a matching closing `)`.
PARENTHESIS_EXPECTED.prevention_advice: Most modern editors auto-close parentheses. Count your opening and closing parentheses when you see this error.

BRACE_EXPECTED.title: Unmatched Curly Brace
BRACE_EXPECTED.beginner_explanation: You missed a closing curly brace `}` or opening curly brace `{` for a class, method, or loop.
BRACE_EXPECTED.why_it_happened: Curly braces define code blocks in Java. A missing brace makes the compiler think the class or method continues indefinitely.
common_causes: Missing `}` at the end of the class or `main` method
Accidental deletion of a brace while editing code
BRACE_EXPECTED.suggested_fix: Add the missing closing brace `}` at the appropriate block boundary.
BRACE_EXPECTED.prevention_advice: Keep your code properly indented. If indentation drifts right without returning left, you are likely missing a closing brace.
